opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Ads and the cost of signing up new customers — the biggest running cost. Up 20% YoY, but a smaller share of sales than a year ago (35% vs 40%).

opex.name: Operations and support
opex.note: Fulfilling orders, running pharmacies and supporting customers. Up 44% YoY as order volumes grew and acquired businesses were added.

opex.name: Technology and development
opex.note: Building the app, website and AI clinical tools, and paying the engineers behind them. Up 45% YoY.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and admin. Up 146% YoY; it includes a $48M legal charge and $29M of acquisition costs (see one-offs).

footerNote: Reports in thousands; figures are rounded to $M (operations and support $96M, exact $95.5M, so the lines add up).

kpis.note: vs $0.17 a year ago — the company made a loss this quarter

kpis.label: International revenue
kpis.note: Up 1,641% YoY, from $8M — the Eucalyptus acquisition closed in June

oneTimers: General and administrative costs include a $48M legal contingencies charge in Q2 alone ($63M in the first half) that the company treats as non-recurring in its Adjusted EBITDA — it is the main reason that line jumped 146% YoY.

General and administrative costs also include $29M of acquisition and transaction-related costs in Q2, largely tied to buying Eucalyptus — an Australian digital-health platform bought for a $969M accounting purchase price ($225M cash up front, the rest deferred and contingent) that closed in June 2026.

Operations and support includes $5M of restructuring and other charges in Q2 ($38M in the first half, including inventory write-downs in cost of revenue in Q1) tied to the company's 2026 shift in its US weight-loss offering toward branded GLP-1 medicines, with compounded GLP-1s offered only on a limited scale.
otherDetail: Other income was $5M, net: a $5M gain from the change in value of equity securities, plus $4M of other income, less a $4M loss from the change in value of liabilities.

segments.name: United States
segments.note: Sales in the US — mostly online telehealth (care by app or phone) for weight loss, hair, skin and other treatments, plus the products that go with them. Up 16%, helped by branded weight-loss offerings; the Hers brand alone was over 40% of US sales.

segments.name: Rest of the world
segments.note: Sales outside the US. Up more than 17-fold, mainly because of recent acquisitions — Eucalyptus, an Australian digital-health platform, closed in June, on top of earlier deals in Europe and Canada.

takeaways.text: Revenue rose 38% to $753M. US sales grew 16% to $622M, while sales outside the US jumped from $8M to $131M after the Eucalyptus deal closed in June. Subscribers reached 2.89M, up 19%, and each subscriber brought in $92 a month on average, up 21%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $3.1B–$3.3B.
takeaways.title: Growth sped up again — mostly abroad

takeaways.text: Gross margin fell from 76% to 64%. The cost of revenue more than doubled, up 112% to $272M, because weight-loss offerings — including GLP-1 drugs (medicines first used for diabetes, now widely used for weight loss) — cost more to buy, package and ship, and ship more often, and the fast-growing international mix costs more to serve.
takeaways.title: Each sale got less profitable

takeaways.text: The bottom line swung from a $43M profit a year ago to an $86M loss. General and administrative costs alone rose $98M, including a $48M legal charge and $29M of deal costs. Leaving out those and similar items, the company's own Adjusted EBITDA measure was still positive at $60M, down from $82M a year ago.
takeaways.title: One-off costs tipped it into a loss

verdict: Hims & Hers grew revenue 38% to $753M as its newly bought international business surged, but higher product costs and a big jump in admin and legal costs swung it to an $86M loss.
